# Sacred Gear Lua API reference

The reference of everything a mod can call, generated from the LuaLS annotations in `gear/meta/`. The guide to writing
a mod (install, events, examples, automation, engine notes) is [Gear.md](Gear.md).

## Editor support (Lua Language Server)

`gear/meta/*.lua` are [LuaLS](https://luals.github.io/) definition files (`---@meta`): they declare the `gear` global,
the objects it returns, the events and callbacks, the options tables, and the manifest of `mod.lua`. With them the
editor completes and checks mod code (VS Code with the "Lua" extension by sumneko, or any editor with LuaLS).

In this repository nothing is needed: `.luarc.json` at the root points LuaLS at `gear/meta`, so the examples in
`gear/examples` get completion and checks.

**In a mod repository** (for instance `sacred-gear-mods`, next to a checkout of this one): copy
`gear/meta/luarc.template.json` to `.luarc.json` in the root of the mod repository and set `workspace.library` to the
`gear/meta` folder (a relative path from that root, or an absolute one). That is all.

What the template sets besides the library:

- `runtime.version` is `LuaJIT`, the Lua Sacred Gear runs.
- `runtime.builtin` hides the libraries a mod does not get: `io`, `debug`, `package`, `jit`, `ffi`, `utf8`, `bit32`, and
  `os`, which `gear/meta/gear.lua` declares again with the four functions mods have (`clock`, `time`, `date`,
  `difftime`). The basic functions a mod lacks (`load`, `loadstring`, `loadfile`, `dofile`, `collectgarbage`,
  `getfenv`, `setfenv`, `newproxy`, `gcinfo`) are declared there as deprecated, so the editor strikes them through.
  What a mod has: `assert error ipairs next pairs pcall rawequal rawget rawset select setmetatable getmetatable
  tonumber tostring type unpack xpcall`, `_VERSION`, `print` and `require` (its own files only), `string`, `table`,
  `math`, `bit`, `coroutine`, and `gear`.

In `mod.lua`, annotate the returned table for completion of the manifest keys:

```lua
---@type GearModManifest
return {
    id = 'hello',
    name = 'Hello, Sacred Gear',
    version = '1.0',
}
```

Handlers get typed arguments from `gear.on`:

```lua
gear.on('frame', function(dt)            -- dt: number
    local hero = gear.world.hero()       -- Creature?
    if hero then print(hero:hp(), hero:class()) end
end)
gear.on('draw', function(state)          -- state: GearUiState
    if state.mode ~= 'game' then return end
    gear.ui.text('Hello', 24, 24, {color = 0xFFFFD080, shadow = true})
end)
```

Not covered by the annotations: values a mod gets from a custom event (`gear.emit` and its handlers take `...`), keys
of `gear.config` (declare your own with `---@type {my_setting: number}` on a local), and the runtime rule that
`gear.auto` exists only in automation runs.

## Maintaining the annotations

The annotations are part of the API: a change to what the Lua side offers is not done until `gear/meta` says so.

1. Change the code (`gear/lua/kernel.lua`, and the native tables in `gear/lua_host.cpp`).
2. Change the matching annotation in `gear/meta/*.lua`: a new function gets a description, `---@param` and
   `---@return` lines; a new field of a table gets a `---@field`; a new option goes into the options class of the
   function; a new event gets a `gear.on` overload and a `GearEventName` entry.
3. Run `python tools/gen_gear_api_docs.py` (rewrites this file) and `python tools/check_gear_api.py` (exit code 0:
   the annotations and the code agree).

`tools/check_gear_api.py` reads `kernel.lua` and `lua_host.cpp` as text and compares names, both ways: a function,
field, event, option or manifest key in the code but not in the annotations, and one in the annotations but not in the
code. It checks names, not types or signatures; those are reviewed by hand. It fails if this file is not what the
generator produces. If the check cannot find a place in the code it expects, the code changed shape: update the
check rather than silence it.

The format of `gear/meta/*.lua`:

- One file per area (`gear.lua`, `data.lua`, `world.lua`, `ui.lua`, `ui_widgets.lua`, `auto.lua`; the list is `FILES`
  in `tools/gear_meta.py`). Every file starts with `---@meta _`.
- `-- ## Title` starts a section of the reference; `--: text` lines right under it are the section's introduction.
  Both are plain comments to LuaLS.
- A namespace or object type is a `---@class` followed by a local table (`local GearWorld = {}`); its functions are
  `function GearWorld.hero() end` (static) or `function Creature:hp() end` (method). The `gear` and `os` globals are
  `gear = {}` and `os = {}` after their class.
- A plain comment `-- path gear.world` right above the class's doc block says how it is reached; the reference prints
  signatures with it (`gear.world.hero()`, `creature:hp()`).
- Options tables are classes whose name ends in `Opts` (`GearTextOpts`); every `opts.x` the kernel reads must be a field
  of one, and `GearPickupRules` holds the keys of `pickup_rules`. Enumerated strings are `---@alias` with `---| 'value' # meaning`.
- Return a value or `nil` and a message as `---@return Creature? creature` and `---@return string? error`.
- Descriptions use the same words as [Gear.md](Gear.md); the guide explains, the reference lists.

To check the examples against the annotations with LuaLS: `lua-language-server --check gear/examples
--configpath .luarc.json` from the repository root (needs the language server installed; not part of the build).

## The gear global

### GearEventName

| Value | |
|---|---|
| `'load'` | All mods are loaded. |
| `'frame'` | Every in-game frame. |
| `'draw'` | After the frame handlers, to draw the UI. |
| `'idle'` | Automation only: every 50 ms in the menus. |
| `'session.start'` | A game with a hero runs. |
| `'session.stop'` | That hero is gone. |
| `'combat.constant'` | The engine loads a pooled float constant inside its own code (hit handlers, difficulty factors ...); a handler may return another number for it. |
| `'creature.ability'` | The creature AI picks the ability (skill or spell id) a creature uses; a handler may return another id. |
| `'level.factor'` | The engine asks for the integer factor of a level (a hook inside its own code; the first handler that returns a number answers). |

### GearHandler

A handler registered with `gear.on`; pass it to `gear.off` to remove it.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `event` | `string` | The event the handler listens to. |
| `fn` | `function` | The handler. |

### GearTimer

A timer started with `gear.after` or `gear.every`; pass it to `gear.cancel`. Opaque.

### GearModInfo

What `gear.mod` tells a mod about itself.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | The manifest's `id`. |
| `name` | `string` | The manifest's `name` (default: the id). |
| `version` | `string` | The manifest's `version` (default `'0'`). |
| `dir` | `string` | The mod's folder name under `mods`. |

### Gear

Reached as `gear`.

The `gear` global: Sacred Gear's API, one copy per mod (each mod has its own globals).

All mod code runs on the engine thread, between the game's update and the drawing of the frame, one handler at a time, so handlers see a consistent state and need no locks.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `string` | Sacred Gear's version. |
| `mod` | `GearModInfo` | This mod's identity. |
| `config` | `table<string, any>` | This mod's settings: the manifest's `config`, overridden by `config.lua`. |
| `data` | `GearData` | The engine's data tables (read only, except the abilities). |
| `text` | `GearText` | The game's texts by id. |
| `settings` | `GearSettings` | The game's Settings.cfg. |
| `files` | `GearFiles` | The mod's file overlay. |
| `game` | `GearGame` | Facts about the running game. |
| `hooks` | `GearHooks` | The engine hooks that ask mods for values. |
| `json` | `GearJson` | JSON encoding and decoding. |
| `pipe` | `GearPipeModule` | Named pipe clients. |
| `world` | `GearWorld` | The world: hero, creatures, items, spawning, pickup rules. |
| `ui` | `GearUi` | Drawing on top of the game, widgets, panels and the layout. |
| `auto` | `GearAuto` | Automation (only with `-gear-auto` and `automation = true` in `mod.lua`). (optional) |

#### `gear.on(event, fn) -> GearHandler`

Calls `fn` for `event`; returns a handle for `gear.off`. Built-in events: see `GearEventName`. Any other name is a custom event that `gear.emit` fires (it has a dot: `twitch.command`).

Forms:

- `fun(event: 'load', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'frame', fn: fun(dt: number)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'draw', fn: fun(state: GearUiState)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'idle', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'session.start', fn: fun(hero: Creature)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'session.stop', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'combat.constant', fn: fun(name: string, vanilla: number, index: integer): number?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'creature.ability', fn: fun(type: integer, vanilla: integer, index: integer, address: integer): integer?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'level.factor', fn: fun(level: number, site: integer): number?): GearHandler`

- `event`: `string`
- `fn`: `fun(...: any)`
- returns `GearHandler`

#### `gear.off(handle)`

Removes a handler.

- `handle`: `GearHandler`

#### `gear.emit(event, ...)`

Calls every handler of a custom event now. Custom names have a dot (`twitch.command`); the built-in events and the prefixes `session.`, `gear.` and `pipe.` are reserved. Handlers may emit events too, up to 8 levels deep.

- `event`: `string`
- `...`: `any`

#### `gear.after(seconds, fn) -> GearTimer`

Runs `fn` once after `seconds` (real seconds while the game runs frames, not in menus or loading screens).

- `seconds`: `number`
- `fn`: `fun()`
- returns `GearTimer`

#### `gear.every(seconds, fn) -> GearTimer`

Runs `fn` every `seconds`. A timer whose function raised an error stops. At most 1000 timers per mod.

- `seconds`: `number` - Greater than 0.
- `fn`: `fun()`
- returns `GearTimer`

#### `gear.cancel(timer)`

Stops a timer.

- `timer`: `GearTimer`

#### `gear.task(fn)`

Runs `fn` as a task: a coroutine that may wait with `gear.wait` and `gear.wait_until` without holding up the frame. It is resumed every tick (in game every frame; with automation in the menus too).

- `fn`: `fun()`

#### `gear.wait(seconds)`

Inside a task: waits `seconds`.

- `seconds`: `number`

#### `gear.wait_until(test, timeout) -> boolean`

Inside a task: waits until `test()` returns true, at most `timeout` seconds.

- `test`: `fun(): boolean`
- `timeout`: `number` (optional) - Default 30.
- returns `satisfied` `boolean` - True when `test()` returned true, false after the timeout.

#### `gear.log(...)`

A line in `SacredGear.log`, prefixed with the mod's id. Same as `print`.

- `...`: `any`

#### `gear.time() -> number`

Seconds, high resolution, from an arbitrary start.

- returns `number`

#### `gear.read(name) -> string?, string?`

Reads a file of the mod's own folder (directly in it, no subfolders).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `text` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.save(name, text) -> boolean?, string?`

Writes a file in the mod's folder, for settings a mod's own UI changes: `*.json`, `*.txt` or `*.lua` other than `mod.lua` and `main.lua`, at most 1 MB.

- `name`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

## The manifest (mod.lua)

### GearModManifest

The table `mod.lua` returns. It runs without any globals, so it can only hold values. Annotate it with `---@type GearModManifest` above the `return`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Required: letters, digits, `_` and `-`; unique among the installed mods. |
| `name` | `string` | Shown in the log (default: the id). (optional) |
| `version` | `string` | Part of the mod set (default `'0'`). (optional) |
| `priority` | `number` | Lower loads first (default 0); ties load by id. (optional) |
| `requires` | `string[]` | Ids that must load first; the mod is skipped if one is missing. (optional) |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `false`: keep the folder, skip the mod. (optional) |
| `config` | `table<string, any>` | Default settings: `gear.config` starts as a copy and `config.lua` overrides them. (optional) |
| `pipes` | `string[]` | Names of the named pipes the mod may open (`gear.pipe.open`). (optional) |
| `automation` | `boolean` | `true`: the mod gets `gear.auto` when the game runs with `-gear-auto`. (optional) |

## The standard library a mod gets

### GearOs

Reached as `os`.

A mod gets `string`, `table`, `math`, `bit`, `coroutine` and the basic functions below, and from `os` only `clock`, `time`, `date` and `difftime`. Each mod has its own globals.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `clock` | `fun(): number` |  |
| `time` | `fun(t?: table): integer` |  |
| `date` | `fun(format?: string, time?: integer): string\|table` |  |
| `difftime` | `fun(t2: integer, t1: integer): number` |  |

#### `require(name) -> any`

Runs `name.lua` of this mod's folder once (`a.b` is `a\b.lua`) and returns its result (`true` if it returns nothing). Only the mod's own files.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `any`

#### `print(...)`

A line in `SacredGear.log`, prefixed with the mod's id. Same as `gear.log`.

- `...`: `any`

#### `load(chunk, chunkname, mode, env)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `loadstring(text, chunkname)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `loadfile(filename)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `dofile(filename)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `collectgarbage(opt, arg)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `getfenv(f)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `setfenv(f, table)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `newproxy(arg)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `gcinfo()`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

## Data tables (gear.data)

### GearData

Reached as `gear.data`.

The engine's data tables: read only, except the abilities.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `object_types` | `GearObjectTypes` | The type records every object refers to (0x80 bytes; id = index, 1..0x7E5F). |
| `creature_types` | `GearTable` | `Pak\Creature.pak`'s records (0x56 bytes). |
| `abilities` | `GearAbilities` | The ability tables of the exe by id (skills, combat arts, spells), which a mod can change. |

### GearRecord

Written `record` in the signatures.

One record of a table, read in place. Fields are read by byte offset; nil if out of range.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `index` | `integer` | The record's index. |

#### `record:u8(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:i8(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:u16(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:i16(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:u32(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:i32(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:f32(offset) -> number?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `number?`

#### `record:str(offset, max_length) -> string?`

A zero-terminated string.

- `offset`: `integer`
- `max_length`: `integer` (optional) - Default 64.
- returns `string?`

### GearTable

Written `records` in the signatures.

A read only table of records.

#### `records:count() -> integer`

The number of records (0 if the table is not available).

- returns `integer`

#### `records:stride() -> integer`

The size of a record in bytes (0 if the table is not available).

- returns `integer`

#### `records:get(index) -> GearRecord?`

Record `index`, counted from 0.

- `index`: `integer`
- returns `record` `GearRecord?` - nil if out of range.

### GearObjectTypes

Reached as `gear.data.object_types`.

Includes everything of `GearTable`.

The object types. Besides the table functions it knows the types by name.

#### `gear.data.object_types:name(id) -> string?`

The internal name of type `id` (nil if it has none).

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:kind(id) -> integer?`

The kind (the type record's byte +0x2E) of type `id`.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:find(name) -> integer?`

The id of the type named `name` (any case; the first type with that name).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:search(text, limit) -> GearTypeMatch[]`

The types whose name contains `text` (plain text, any case), ordered by id.

- `text`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer` (optional) - Default 100.
- returns `GearTypeMatch[]`

### GearTypeMatch

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `kind` | `integer` |  (optional) |

## Abilities (gear.data.abilities)

### GearAbilities

Reached as `gear.data.abilities`.

The exe's two ability tables as one table by id: T1 (the combat arts: ids from 1000, 0x78-byte records) and T2 (the spells: ids from 1, 0x94-byte records). `abilities[id]` is the record of ability `id` (nil if there is none); its fields read and write by name. A field has a name where code that uses it proves what it is, and is `unk_<offset>` (in hex) otherwise. Writes go to the live tables, are checked for type and range, and are undone with `restore` (and when the mod is switched off).

#### `gear.data.abilities:ids() -> integer[]`

The ids of all abilities, ascending.

- returns `integer[]`

#### `gear.data.abilities:fields(id) -> GearAbilityField[]?`

The fields of the table that ability `id` is in, ordered by offset.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `fields` `GearAbilityField[]?` - nil if there is no such ability.

#### `gear.data.abilities:apply(edits) -> integer?, string[]?`

Writes many fields at once: `{[id] = {field = value, ...}}`. Everything is checked first; if any id, field or value is wrong nothing is written and the problems are returned.

- `edits`: `table<integer, table<string, number>>`
- returns `written` `integer?` - The number of fields written (nil if nothing was).
- returns `problems` `string[]?` - What was wrong.

#### `gear.data.abilities:restore() -> integer`

Undoes this mod's writes to the ability tables.

- returns `restored` `integer` - The number of fields restored.

### GearAbilityField

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `offset` | `integer` | The byte offset in the record. |
| `kind` | `string` | `'u8'`, `'i16'`, `'f32'` ... |

### GearAbility

Written `ability` in the signatures.

One ability record. Reading a field of a table the ability is not in (or an unknown name) gives nil; writing one is an error, as is writing a value that does not fit the field or the `id`. Both have `id`, `name_text`, `description_text`, `target_mode` and the `unk_` fields; T1 also `effect_base`, `effect_per_level`, `effect2_base` and `effect2_per_level`; T2 also `value0_base` .. `value3_per_level`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | `string` | `'T1'` or `'T2'`. |
| `index` | `integer` | The record's index in its table. |
| `kind` | `string` | `'combat_art'` (T1: ids from 1000) or `'spell'` (T2: ids from 1): what the names in the game's texts say they are. |
| `id` | `integer` | The ability's id. |
| `name_text` | `integer` | The text id of the name (`gear.text.get`). |
| `description_text` | `integer` | The text id of the description. |
| `target_mode` | `integer` | How the ability is aimed (the engine passes it on to the targeting code). |
| `effect_base` | `number` | T1: the first effect is `effect_base + level * effect_per_level` (level 1..100). |
| `effect_per_level` | `number` | T1. |
| `effect2_base` | `number` | T1: the second effect. |
| `effect2_per_level` | `number` | T1. |
| `value0_base` | `integer` | T2: the first value is `value0_base + level * value0_per_level`. |
| `value0_per_level` | `integer` | T2. |
| `value1_base` | `integer` | T2. |
| `value1_per_level` | `integer` | T2. |
| `value2_base` | `integer` | T2. |
| `value2_per_level` | `integer` | T2. |
| `value3_base` | `integer` | T2. |
| `value3_per_level` | `integer` | T2. |

## Game text (gear.text)

### GearText

Reached as `gear.text`.

The game's own texts, by the text ids its data tables hold (not the keys of `global.res`).

#### `gear.text.get(id) -> string?`

The text for `id` (UTF-8), nil if the game has none.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `string?`

## Settings (gear.settings)

### GearSettings

Reached as `gear.settings`.

The game's `Settings.cfg` (`KEY : value` lines).

#### `gear.settings.get(key) -> string?`

The value of `key` as text (nil if the file has no such key). Read each time, so it is what the file says now.

- `key`: `string`
- returns `string?`

## Files (gear.files)

### GearFiles

Reached as `gear.files`.

The file overlay: a mod's own data files served where the game opens the original ones, and the mod's own save folder. Declared in `mods/<id>/overlay.txt` (`game\path = dataile` per line, `saves = save`), read when Sacred Gear starts because the game opens its data files before any Lua runs. See [Gear.md](Gear.md).

#### `gear.files.overlay() -> GearOverlayInfo?`

What this mod's overlay does, nil if the mod has no `overlay.txt` (or the run does not use it).

- returns `GearOverlayInfo?`

#### `gear.files.resolve(path) -> string`

The path the game's open of `path` (relative to the game folder) ends up at: the mod's file if an overlay rule applies, else `path` unchanged.

- `path`: `string`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.files.served(path) -> integer`

How many times the game opened `path` (relative to the game folder) and was served a mod's file by the overlay.

- `path`: `string`
- returns `integer`

### GearOverlayInfo

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `files` | `integer` | The number of file rules. |
| `saves` | `string` | The mod's save folder (absolute) if the game's `Save\` folder is redirected to it. (optional) |

## Engine hooks (gear.hooks)

### GearHooks

Reached as `gear.hooks`.

The engine hooks that ask mods for a value inside the game's own code (see the events `level.factor`).

#### `gear.hooks.stats(name) -> GearHookStats`

The counters of a hook since the game started: how often the engine asked, how often a mod answered, and how often Lua could not take the question (busy: it was running on this or another thread, so the engine kept its own value).

- `name`: `'level.factor'|'combat.constant'|'creature.ability'`
- returns `GearHookStats`

#### `gear.hooks.sites() -> GearHookSite[]`

Every hook site and how often the engine ran it (a site whose function was not found or whose code did not match is listed with address 0).

- returns `GearHookSite[]`

### GearHookSite

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `hook` | `string` | The hook's name (`level.factor`, or the name of a `combat.constant`). |
| `index` | `integer` | The place among those of that name. |
| `address` | `integer` | Where the site is in the game. |
| `calls` | `integer` | How many times the engine ran the site. |

### GearHookStats

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `calls` | `integer` |  |
| `answered` | `integer` |  |
| `busy` | `integer` |  |

## The running game (gear.game)

### GearGame

Reached as `gear.game`.

Facts about the running game.

#### `gear.game.difficulty() -> integer?`

The difficulty level of the running game: 0 (bronze) to 4 (niobium); nil if the game is not running.

- returns `integer?`

## JSON (gear.json)

### GearJson

Reached as `gear.json`.

Objects are tables with string keys, arrays tables with the keys 1..n.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | `table` | Stands for JSON null (`decode` gives it for null values in arrays and objects). |

#### `gear.json.encode(value) -> string`

Encodes a value as JSON text. Errors for functions, NaN, infinity and keys that are not strings.

- `value`: `any`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.json.decode(text) -> any?, string?`

Decodes JSON text.

- `text`: `string`

## Named pipes (gear.pipe)

### GearPipeModule

Reached as `gear.pipe`.

Named pipe clients.

#### `gear.pipe.open(name) -> GearPipe`

A client of `\\.\pipe\<name>`; the name must be listed in `pipes` in `mod.lua`. The client reconnects by itself. Messages are framed with a 16-bit little-endian length (the risen-twitch / Gothic Twitch connector's format).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `GearPipe`

### GearPipe

Written `pipe` in the signatures.

A pipe client. Set `on_message`, `on_connect` and `on_disconnect` to receive.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `on_message` | `fun(text: string)` | Called for each message received. (optional) |
| `on_connect` | `fun()` | Called when the connection is made. (optional) |
| `on_disconnect` | `fun()` | Called when it is lost. (optional) |

#### `pipe:send(text) -> boolean`

Sends a message; false if the pipe is closed or not connected.

- `text`: `string`
- returns `boolean`

#### `pipe:connected() -> boolean`

- returns `boolean`

#### `pipe:close()`

Closes the pipe for good.

### GearWorld

Reached as `gear.world`.

Positions are world units (`TILE`, about 53.7, is one tile; the screen shows about 534 x 400 around the hero) and a layer (0 outdoors; dungeons have their own). The functions that change the world work only in single player (`can_change()`); in a network game they return nil and a message.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `TILE` | `number` | World units per tile. |
| `CLASSES` | `GearClassInfo[]` | The hero classes. |
| `QUALITIES` | `GearQuality[]` | Item qualities in ascending order; `quality_rank` is the index. |

#### `gear.world.spawn(type, x, y, opts) -> Creature?, string?`

Creates an object of `type` (a type id or an object type name) at (x, y), as the game's own scripts do. Single player only.

#### `gear.world.pickup_rules(rules)`

Sets this mod's pickup rules, replacing its previous ones (`nil`: none). The local hero does not pick up the `block` items (a click on them does nothing, the automatic collecting passes them by), and the ground labels of the `dim` items are drawn with their alpha scaled to `dim_alpha`. The rules of all mods are merged after each tick. They hold in single player and for the host's own hero. Item ids are only valid while the item exists.

- `rules`: `GearPickupRules` (optional)

#### `gear.world.pickup_refused() -> integer`

The number of pickups refused so far.

- returns `integer`

## Drawing (gear.ui)

### GearColor

A color: an `0xAARRGGBB` number (see `gear.ui.rgba`), `{r, g, b, a}` or `{r = , g = , b = , a = }` (0..255, `a` defaults to 255).

`integer|integer[]|{r: integer, g: integer, b: integer, a: integer?}`

### GearLayer

Where in the game's draw order. `world`: in game, over the world and under every window. `hud` (default): over the game's windows, under tooltips, the escape menu and message boxes. `top`: over everything but the cursor and its tooltip.

`'world'|'hud'|'top'`

### GearTextAlign

`'left'|'center'|'right'`

### GearTextVAlign

`'top'|'middle'|'bottom'|'baseline'`

### GearImageFit

`'stretch'|'contain'|'cover'|'fit'|'fill'`

### GearDrawOpts

Options of every draw function.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | `GearLayer` | Default `'hud'`. (optional) |
| `window` | `string` | A control name (`UI_WND_INVENTORY`): the command is drawn in that window's coordinates and frame, so it moves with the window, and clipped to its 1024x768 frame; nothing is drawn while the window does not exist. (optional) |

### GearTextOpts

Includes everything of `GearDrawOpts`.

Options of `gear.ui.text` (and the font options of widgets and `text_size`).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | `GearColor` | Default white. (optional) |
| `font` | `'ui'\|'game1'\|'game2'\|'game3'\|'game4'\|'game5'\|'game6'\|'game7'\|integer` | Default: the vector UI font (Segoe UI). `'game1'`..`'game7'` (or the number 1..7; 0 is a debug font) draw in the game's own bitmap font, scaled with the UI. (optional) |
| `size` | `number` | The em height in layout units (vector font; default 13). (optional) |
| `face` | `string` | A Windows font name (vector font). (optional) |
| `bold` | `boolean` | Vector font. (optional) |
| `italic` | `boolean` | Vector font. (optional) |
| `shadow` | `boolean` | Vector font: a dark 1 pixel shadow. (optional) |
| `outline` | `boolean` | Vector font: a dark 1 pixel outline. (optional) |
| `width` | `number` | The box width, for `align`. (optional) |
| `height` | `number` | The box height, for `valign`. (optional) |
| `align` | `GearTextAlign` | Aligns in `width`. (optional) |
| `valign` | `GearTextVAlign` | Aligns in `height`; `'middle'` puts the capitals' middle on the box's, `'baseline'`: y is the first line's baseline. (optional) |
| `background` | `GearColor` | A rectangle behind the text, sized to it. (optional) |
| `padding` | `number` | Around the text, with `background`. (optional) |
| `markup` | `boolean` | Game fonts: pass their backslash codes (`\c` color, `\g` image) through; otherwise a `\` shows as `/`. (optional) |
| `flags` | `integer` | Raw font flags of the game's font (or-ed into `align`). (optional) |

### GearImageOpts

Includes everything of `GearDrawOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `fit` | `GearImageFit` | `'stretch'` (default: fills the box), `'contain'` (the whole image, aspect kept, centered), `'cover'` (fills the box, aspect kept, the overhang cut off). (optional) |
| `color` | `GearColor` | Tint: white as is; the alpha makes it translucent. (optional) |

### GearImageInfo

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The game's image index (stable for a build). |
| `sheet` | `string` | The sheet's TGA name. |
| `width` | `integer` |  |
| `height` | `integer` |  |
| `loaded` | `boolean` |  |

### GearUi

Reached as `gear.ui`.

Drawing is immediate mode: what a mod draws during a tick (its `draw` and `frame` handlers, timers, tasks) is shown until the next tick replaces it, so a mod draws its overlay every frame, usually in a `draw` handler. Without a tick (a loading screen, the menus without automation) nothing is drawn after half a second.

Positions and sizes are the UI's 1024x768 layout, the space the game lays its windows out in; the game and SacredBild scale it to the screen. A mod may issue 2000 draw commands per tick (widgets count their rectangles and texts).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `WIDTH` | `integer` | 1024 |
| `HEIGHT` | `integer` | 768 |
| `COLORS` | `GearColors` | The widgets' colours. |

### GearColors

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` | `integer` |  |
| `bg_hover` | `integer` |  |
| `bg_down` | `integer` |  |
| `edge` | `integer` |  |
| `edge_dim` | `integer` |  |
| `text` | `integer` |  |
| `text_dim` | `integer` |  |
| `accent` | `integer` |  |
| `title` | `integer` |  |

#### `gear.ui.rgba(r, g, b, a) -> integer`

The color number `0xAARRGGBB` (`a` defaults to 255).

- `r`: `integer`
- `g`: `integer`
- `b`: `integer`
- `a`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `integer`

#### `gear.ui.rect(x, y, w, h, color, opts) -> boolean`

A filled rectangle (default color: black, 75 % opaque). Edges snap to the screen's pixels.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `color`: `GearColor` (optional)
- `opts`: `GearDrawOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean` - False when nothing was drawn (its `window` does not exist).

#### `gear.ui.frame(x, y, w, h, color, thickness, opts) -> boolean`

An outline inside the box.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `color`: `GearColor` (optional)
- `thickness`: `number` (optional) - Default 1.
- `opts`: `GearDrawOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.text(text, x, y, opts) -> boolean`

Text, UTF-8, lines break at `\n`. By default in a vector UI font (Segoe UI) rasterized for the screen's pixels, so it stays sharp however far the UI is scaled.

- `text`: `any` - Converted with `tostring`.
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearTextOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.image(id, x, y, w, h, opts) -> boolean`

A UI image; `w`, `h` default to its own size. Images are filtered linearly.

- `id`: `integer` - An id from `images`.
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number` (optional)
- `h`: `number` (optional)
- `opts`: `GearImageOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.images(filter) -> GearImageInfo[]`

The UI images whose sheet name contains `filter` (any case), all of them without a filter.

- `filter`: `string` (optional)
- returns `GearImageInfo[]`

#### `gear.ui.image_info(id) -> GearImageInfo?`

One UI image, or nil.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `GearImageInfo?`

#### `gear.ui.fonts() -> integer`

The number of the game's UI fonts.

- returns `integer`

#### `gear.ui.text_size(text, font) -> number?, number?`

Width and height of the text in the layout, or nil. Game fonts in game only (measuring may add glyphs to the font).

- `text`: `any`
- `font`: `'ui'|'game1'|'game2'|'game3'|'game4'|'game5'|'game6'|'game7'|integer|GearTextOpts` (optional) - A game font, or a table of `text`'s font options; nil: the default UI font.
- returns `width` `number?`

## Widgets and input

Widgets are immediate mode too: call them every frame with the current values; each draws itself, takes the mouse over its rectangle and returns what the player did since the last frame. `id` names the widget within the mod (any string or number, unique per widget). Positions are canvas coordinates (not `opts.window`).

### GearWidgetOpts

Options every widget takes.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `tooltip` | `string` | Shown after the cursor rests on the widget for 0.4 s. (optional) |
| `layer` | `GearLayer` | Default `'hud'`. (optional) |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `false`: greyed out, no clicks. (optional) |

| `face` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `bold` | `boolean` |  (optional) |
| `italic` | `boolean` |  (optional) |
| `height` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `valign` | `GearTextVAlign` |  (optional) |
| `color` | `GearColor` |  (optional) |

## Layout: persistent panels, movable game windows

Every panel has the id `mod_id:panel_id`. Where the player drags it (and how large they make it, with `opts.resizable`) is kept in `mods\gear_layout.json` and restored at the next start. Places are stored in a virtual 4096 x 4096 screen (the whole screen, whatever its resolution and aspect). The game's own windows are kept there too, as `game:UI_WND_INVENTORY` and so on. Moving game windows needs SacredBild's UI frames.

### GearPanelInfo

A panel as `gear.ui.panels` lists it.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `mod` | `string` |  |
| `id` | `string\|integer` |  |
| `title` | `string` |  |
| `x` | `number` |  |
| `y` | `number` |  |
| `w` | `number` |  |
| `h` | `number` |  |
| `resizable` | `boolean` |  |
| `min_width` | `number` |  |
| `min_height` | `number` |  |
| `layer` | `GearLayer` |  |

### GearLayoutEntry

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `number` | In virtual units. |
| `y` | `number` |  |
| `w` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `h` | `number` |  (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.edit_mode() -> boolean`

The layout edit mode flag, for every mod (panels get a highlighted frame).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.set_edit_mode(on)`

- `on`: `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.can_move_windows() -> boolean`

Whether the game's windows can be moved (needs SacredBild's UI frames).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.panels() -> GearPanelInfo[]`

The panels of every mod drawn this tick (those not drawn yet: as of the last tick).

- returns `GearPanelInfo[]`

#### `gear.ui.set_panel_rect(key, x, y, w, h) -> boolean`

Puts any mod's panel at (x, y) of the canvas and, if it is resizable, makes it w x h (nil: the size stays); kept in the layout, taken the next time its mod draws it.

- `key`: `string`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number` (optional)
- `h`: `number` (optional)
- returns `found` `boolean` - False for an unknown panel.

#### `gear.ui.reset_panel(key) -> boolean`

A panel back to the place and size its mod gives it.

- `key`: `string`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.set_window_position(name, x, y) -> boolean`

Puts game window `name` with its top-left corner at (x, y) of the canvas and keeps it in the layout. Any in-game window but those the game draws alone (world map, savegame, options, character export).

- `name`: `string`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.reset_window(name) -> boolean`

A game window back to its own place.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.reset_layout(prefix)`

Forgets all places, or those whose key starts with `prefix` (e.g. `'game:'`).

- `prefix`: `string` (optional)

#### `gear.ui.layout() -> table<string, GearLayoutEntry>`

The stored places.

- returns `table<string, GearLayoutEntry>`

#### `gear.ui.to_virtual(x, y) -> number, number`

From the canvas to the virtual 4096 x 4096 screen.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `vx` `number`
- returns `vy` `number`

#### `gear.ui.from_virtual(vx, vy) -> number, number`

- `vx`: `number`
- `vy`: `number`
- returns `x` `number`
- returns `y` `number`

### GearAuto

Reached as `gear.auto`.

For self tests and scripted runs without a player. `gear.auto` exists only when the game starts with `-gear-auto` (or `SACREDGEAR_AUTO=1`) and the mod's manifest says `automation = true`. The functions marked "in a task" wait, so they work only inside `gear.task`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `VK` | `table<string, integer>` | Key names to virtual key codes. |
| `instance` | `string` | The run's name (`-gear-instance`). |

#### `gear.auto.state() -> GearAutoState`

- returns `GearAutoState`

#### `gear.auto.ui() -> GearAutoUiNode[]`

The visible UI.

- returns `GearAutoUiNode[]`

#### `gear.auto.move(x, y)`

Moves the game's cursor; client pixels.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`

#### `gear.auto.down(button)`

- `button`: `GearMouseButton` (optional) - Default `'lbutton'`.

#### `gear.auto.up(button)`

- `button`: `GearMouseButton` (optional) - Default `'lbutton'`.

#### `gear.auto.key_down(key)`

- `key`: `GearAutoKey`

#### `gear.auto.key_up(key)`

- `key`: `GearAutoKey`

#### `gear.auto.release()`

Releases everything held.

#### `gear.auto.click(x, y, button)`

In a task: moves, presses and releases with short pauses, as a player would. Client pixels.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `button`: `GearMouseButton` (optional)

#### `gear.auto.press(key)`

In a task: presses and releases a key.

- `key`: `GearAutoKey`

#### `gear.auto.type(text)`

In a task: types text, one character at a time.

- `text`: `string`

#### `gear.auto.ui_to_pixels(x, y) -> integer?, integer|string?`

In a task: the client pixel for the UI layout point (x, y); the mapping is measured once by moving the cursor.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `px` `integer?`
- returns `py` `integer|string?` - The pixel, or the error message when `px` is nil.

#### `gear.auto.ui_click(x, y, button) -> boolean?, string?`

In a task: clicks a point in UI layout coordinates, or a node's center.

- `x`: `number|GearAutoUiNode`
- `y`: `number|GearMouseButton` (optional) - With a node: the button.
- `button`: `GearMouseButton` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.auto.load_save(slot) -> boolean?`

Loads savegame `slot` from the menus.

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.screenshot(name) -> boolean?`

Saves a screenshot (`.bmp`) of the game's back buffer into `GearAutomation\<instance>`. Name: letters, digits, `_ - .`.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.engine_level_factor_start(level) -> boolean`

Starts the engine's own level function on a worker thread (the first of the `level.factor` hooks): the call goes through the hook, so a mod that handles `level.factor` answers it. For tests.

- `level`: `integer`
- returns `started` `boolean` - false if a call is running or the function was not found.

#### `gear.auto.engine_level_factor_result() -> integer?`

The integer the call started by `engine_level_factor_start` returned; nil until it is done.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.auto.site_hook_selftest_start() -> boolean`

Tests the stubs of the constant site hooks on two functions built in memory (`fmul dword [c]` and `fld dword [c]`, with the sites `selftest.fmul` and `selftest.fld` of the event `combat.constant`); a worker thread calls them when Lua is idle.

- returns `started` `boolean` - false if a test is running.

#### `gear.auto.site_hook_selftest_result() -> {fmul: number, fld: number, registers_kept: boolean}?`

The result of the test: `fmul` and `fld` are st0 after the instruction (the answer of the mods, else vanilla 0.2 and 0.2 times 1.0), `registers_kept` whether eax, ecx and edx survived the stub. nil until it is done.

- returns `{fmul: number, fld: number, registers_kept: boolean}?`

#### `gear.auto.write(name, text) -> boolean?`

Writes a file into `GearAutomation\<instance>`.

- `name`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.quit(code)`

Ends the game at once with that exit code.

- `code`: `integer` (optional) - Default 0.

#### `gear.auto.wait_for_menu(timeout) -> boolean`

In a task: waits until the main menu is up.

- `timeout`: `number` (optional) - Default 120.
- returns `up` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.wait_for_game(timeout) -> boolean`

In a task: waits until a game with a hero runs.

- `timeout`: `number` (optional) - Default 180.
- returns `running` `boolean`
